Sowing Dates: Extensible Onset Detection in aquacropr

Source: vignettes/sowingdate.Rmd
sowingdate.Rmd

Overview

AquaCrop requires a planting date for each simulation year. For rainfed crops, this date is often derived from the onset of the rainy season.

The AquaCrop standalone provides a fixed set of criteria for determining this onset. These criteria cover common rainfall- and temperature-based rules, but they cannot represent every agronomic definition of the beginning of a growing season.

This becomes important in rainfall-limited environments. In the Sahel, for example, the first substantial rainfall event may be followed by a long dry spell. A rainfall threshold can therefore identify a date that is meteorologically plausible but unsuitable for crop establishment.

aquacropr addresses both issues by moving onset detection into R.

The package reproduces the native AquaCrop criteria, but is not limited to them. The same framework can implement onset definitions based on rainfall accumulation, dry spells, temperature, multiple conditions, or other indicators derived from daily climate data.

Three additional methods are currently implemented for Sahelian applications: Sivakumar (1988), Marteau et al. (2009), and a fuzzy criterion based on Waongo et al. (2014). They illustrate the main added value of the approach: the onset criterion becomes extensible, while the resulting simulation remains compatible with AquaCrop.

This vignette describes the onset engine, the available criteria, and the principles for extending it.

Reproducibility

Code in this vignette is shown but not executed. The complete dataset used to reproduce the examples is distributed separately because the archive is approximately 1 GB.

Data: hosted on OSF as TEST.zip (<OSF_DIRECT_DOWNLOAD_URL> – see the “Regional Crop Simulations” vignette’s “Download the example dataset” section for the download code and archive contents).

From an AquaCrop criterion to an extensible onset engine

The AquaCrop workflow

The .CAL file describes how the beginning of the growing season should be determined.

In the AquaCrop GUI, this information is used to derive sowing dates before the project master file (.PRM) is written. For the standalone simulation, the essential result is the planting date stored in the .PRM.

This creates a useful separation between two tasks:

  1. determining when planting should occur; and
  2. simulating the crop from that planting date.

aquacropr uses this separation to make the first task extensible.

The aquacropr approach

find_onset() implements onset detection in R.

It reads the .CAL configuration and the required climate data, applies the selected criterion to each year, and returns the corresponding planting dates.

write_prm() uses the same engine to place these dates in the .PRM file expected by AquaCrop.

The simulation itself does not need to know how the planting date was obtained.

This is the key design choice.

A planting date can come from a native AquaCrop criterion, a published agroclimatic definition, or a more specialized rule implemented in aquacropr. Once the date has been determined, the downstream AquaCrop workflow is unchanged.

The package therefore preserves compatibility with AquaCrop while removing the onset calculation from a fixed set of criteria.

This architecture also makes onset detection easier to inspect and test. The dates can be examined before a crop simulation is launched.

aquacropr::write_cal(
  site_name = "Ouaga",
  onset = "rainfall",
  window_start = 100,
  window_length = 120,
  criterion = 2,
  preset_value = 20,
  successive_days = 3
)

aquacropr::find_onset("Ouaga")

aquacropr::write_prm(
  site_name = "Ouaga",
  ...
)

Calling find_onset() explicitly is optional. It is useful when onset dates need to be inspected, compared, or validated before running the simulation.

Available onset methods

The current implementation supports fixed, rainfall, and thermal onset.

onset Climate file Typical use
"fixed" .PLU Prescribed planting date
"rainfall" .PLU Rainfed crops
"thermal" .Tnx Temperature-limited seasons

Within these types, aquacropr reproduces the native AquaCrop criteria and adds methods that are not available in the standalone.

Method Main information used AquaCrop standalone
Native criteria 1–4 Rainfall or temperature Yes
Sivakumar (1988) Rainfall + subsequent dry spell No
Marteau et al. (2009) Planting rainfall + subsequent dry spell No
Fuzzy criterion Rainfall + wet days + dry-spell risk No

The distinction between native and additional criteria is important, but the framework is not restricted to the methods in this table.

A new onset definition can combine any information available to the onset engine. For example, a criterion could incorporate several rainfall thresholds, antecedent conditions, dry-spell characteristics, temperature, evapotranspiration, or other climate-derived indicators.

The current Sahelian methods should therefore be viewed both as useful criteria in their own right and as examples of what becomes possible once onset detection is handled in R.

Why additional criteria matter

An onset criterion is an operational definition of a planting opportunity.

Different definitions answer different questions.

A cumulative rainfall criterion asks whether enough rain has fallen.

A multi-day criterion asks whether enough rain has fallen within a short period.

A rainfall-to-ETo criterion also considers atmospheric demand.

A false-start criterion asks an additional question: whether favourable conditions persist after the candidate planting date.

A fuzzy criterion can go further by allowing several indicators to contribute gradually rather than making the decision depend on a single hard threshold.

These differences matter in the Sahel because early-season rainfall is highly variable. A substantial rainfall event can trigger germination and still be followed by conditions unable to sustain crop establishment.

The additional methods in aquacropr demonstrate how the same AquaCrop simulation can be driven by onset definitions adapted to this type of agroclimatic problem.

Extending the onset framework

The three additional methods are not intended to define the limit of the onset engine.

They demonstrate three forms of extension:

  • Sivakumar adds a condition after the initial rainfall trigger;
  • Marteau represents an onset definition informed by observed planting behaviour;
  • the fuzzy criterion combines several indicators through continuous membership functions rather than hard thresholds.

Other definitions can follow the same principle.

For example, future criteria could use soil-water conditions, different dry-spell definitions, crop-specific establishment requirements, or locally calibrated combinations of climate indicators.

The important point is that these extensions affect the calculation of the planting date, not the AquaCrop simulation interface.

As long as the onset engine produces a valid planting date for each simulation year, write_prm() can pass that result to AquaCrop in the same way.

This makes onset detection a modular part of the aquacropr workflow rather than a closed list of planting rules.
